title: backlog.py new refuses a genuine repro whose tool under test has a SyntaxError or passes on exit 127
goal: own_failure counts a SyntaxError as the repro's own only when it is in the -c code or a script the repro wrote for itself, not in a repository tool the repro runs (a portability defect such as a 3.12-only construct on 3.11 is a genuine repro); exit 127 or 9009 from a wrapper (bash script, hook) whose own output shows a tool inside it was not found is accepted; and python3 -u, -X, and sh -c forms are read for the script they run. Found by the SP-2agxqrrv review.

run: import sys, subprocess, tempfile; sys.path.insert(0, '_tools'); import backlog as b; sys.exit(0 if b.own_failure(['python3', '_tools/rag.py', 'pack', 'x'], 1, '  File "_tools/rag.py", line 3\n    x = (\nSyntaxError: invalid syntax') is None else 1)
